key_insight: A spectral interface-evolution model captures fluid-fluid displacement dynamics and energy dissipation in rough fractures beyond the quasistatic regime.
engineering_relevance: The method enables more tractable prediction of hysteresis and dissipation in fractured and porous-media flows, supporting better upscaling for subsurface and multiphase-flow applications.
method: Spectral computational approach for evolving fluid interfaces in a variable-aperture Hele-Shaw fracture.
Validates against computational fluid dynamics simulations and experiments.
Analyzes both a single defect and random roughness across many time and length scales.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement with CFD simulations and experiments, and demonstrates efficiency on cases with a single defect and random roughness spanning many orders of magnitude in time.
watch_item: The approach is validated on a model rough-fracture system, so transfer to fully realistic porous media may require additional geometry, physics, and scale-up checks.
paper_title: Dynamics of fluid-fluid displacements in a model rough fracture beyond the quasistatic limit: A spectral approach
